narrative.title: The Ticket-Queue Deadlock Scanner
narrative.scenario: A batch job runner processes work items whose one-way 'wait for' tickets must never form a loop. The scanner peels the system like an onion: any item nobody waits on (indegree zero) runs and cancels its own outgoing tickets, freeing more items. If the peeling stops with items still stuck holding tickets, a circular wait — a deadlock — is proven.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer V and an adjacency list adj where adj[i] lists the items that item i's completion unblocks.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the directed graph contains a cycle, otherwise false.

testCases.explanation: Every item eventually reaches indegree zero — the whole queue drains cleanly.
Each item waits on the next in a closed ring; nothing ever reaches indegree zero.

hintLevels: Level 1: Repeatedly remove items with nothing pending on them; watch whether anything survives.
Level 2: Maintain indegree counters; enqueue zeros, and decrement successors as each item is removed.
Level 3: A DAG releases exactly V items — any shortfall is the size proof of a cycle.
